definitions.english: A loan is money you borrow and agree to pay back later.
definitions.sesotho: Kalimo ke chelete eo o e alimang mme o dumela ho e kgutlisa hamorao.

definitions.english: When you borrow money, that is called a loan.
definitions.sesotho: Ha o alima chelete, seo se bitswa kalimo.

definitions.english: A loan is money someone gives you that you must return.
definitions.sesotho: Kalimo ke chelete eo motho a o fang yona eo o tlamehang ho e kgutlisa.

definitions.english: Borrowing M50 from a friend is a loan.
definitions.sesotho: Ho alima M50 ho motswalle ke kalimo.

definitions.english: A loan is like borrowing a book — you give it back.
definitions.sesotho: Kalimo e tshwana le ho alima buka — o a e kgutlisa.

definitions.english: A loan is borrowed money repaid with interest over time.
definitions.sesotho: Kalimo ke chelete e alimilweng e kgutliswang le phaello.

definitions.english: Loans can be secured or unsecured.
definitions.sesotho: Dikoloto di ka ba tse sireleditsweng kapa tse sa sireleditsweng.

definitions.english: Student loans help pay for education.
definitions.sesotho: Dikoloto tsa baithuti di thusa ho lefella thuto.

definitions.english: The cost of a loan includes interest and fees.
definitions.sesotho: Theko ya kalimo e kenyelletsa phaello le ditefiso.

definitions.english: Repayment terms define how long you have to repay.
definitions.sesotho: Dipehelo tsa tefo di hlalosa hore na o na le nako e kae ya ho kgutlisa.

definitions.english: Loans are debt instruments requiring repayment with interest.
definitions.sesotho: Dikoloto ke disebediswa tsa molato tse hlokang ho kgutlisa le phaello.

definitions.english: Key metrics include APR and debt-to-income ratio.
definitions.sesotho: Ditekanyo tsa bohlokwa di kenyelletsa APR le debt-to-income ratio.

definitions.english: Amortization schedules split payments between principal and interest.
definitions.sesotho: Mananeo a amortization a arola ditefo pakeng tsa chelete le phaello.

definitions.english: Credit risk determines loan eligibility and rates.
definitions.sesotho: Kotsi ya mokitlane e etsa qeto ya ho tshwaneleha le diphaello.

definitions.english: Student loans may offer deferment and income-based repayment.
definitions.sesotho: Dikoloto tsa baithuti di ka fana ka deferment le ditefo tse itshetlehileng moputsong.

examples.english: Borrow M50 from a friend. You must give back M50.
examples.sesotho: Alima M50 ho motswalle. O tlameha ho kgutlisa M50.

examples.english: Borrow M20 and repay M22. The extra M2 is interest.
examples.sesotho: Alima M20 mme o kgutlise M22. M2 e eketsehileng ke phaello.

examples.english: A bank loan of M100 means you owe the bank M100 plus interest.
examples.sesotho: Kalimo ya banka ya M100 e bolela hore o kolota banka M100 le phaello.

examples.english: A toy costs M60. You borrow M60 and repay from allowance.
examples.sesotho: Sebapadiswa se bitsa M60. O alima M60 mme o kgutlisa ho tswa cheleteng ya pokotho.

examples.english: Borrowing is a promise to return something. Always keep your promise!
examples.sesotho: Ho alima ke tshepiso ya ho kgutlisa. Dula o phethahatsa tshepiso!

examples.english: Student loan of M10,000 at 8 percent over 2 years = M450 monthly.
examples.sesotho: Kalimo ya moithuti ya M10,000 ka 8% dilemo tse 2 = M450 ka kgwedi.

examples.english: Borrow M5,000 for business at 12 percent = repay M5,600.
examples.sesotho: Alima M5,000 bakeng sa kgwebo ka 12% = kgutlisa M5,600.

examples.english: Phone on credit M3,000 at 15 percent over 12 months = M3,450 total.
examples.sesotho: Fono ka mokitlane M3,000 ka 15% dikgwedi tse 12 = M3,450 yohle.

examples.english: Personal loan M2,000 for school fees at 10 percent over 6 months.
examples.sesotho: Kalimo ya botho M2,000 bakeng sa ditefello tsa sekolo ka 10% dikgwedi tse 6.

examples.english: Family loans may have no interest but are still commitments.
examples.sesotho: Dikoloto tsa lelapa di ka se be le phaello empa e ntse e le boitlamo.

examples.english: M15,000 loan at 10 percent over 3 years = M19,500 total.
examples.sesotho: Kalimo ya M15,000 ka 10% dilemo tse 3 = M19,500 yohle.

examples.english: Bank A: 8% for 2 years is cheaper than Bank B: 6% for 3 years.
examples.sesotho: Banka A: 8% dilemo tse 2 e theko e tlase ho feta Banka B: 6% dilemo tse 3.

examples.english: Debt-to-income of 30 percent on M3,000 income = M900 debt payments.
examples.sesotho: Debt-to-income ya 30% ho moputso wa M3,000 = M900 ditefo tsa molato.

examples.english: M20,000 loan at 12 percent over 5 years = M445 monthly.
examples.sesotho: Kalimo ya M20,000 ka 12% dilemo tse 5 = M445 ka kgwedi.

examples.english: Interest-free periods avoid interest if paid within 30 days.
examples.sesotho: Dinako tse se nang phaello di qoba phaello haeba o lefa ka hara matsatsi a 30.

misconceptions.english: You do not have to pay back loans — FALSE! Always repay.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ha o tlamehe ho kgutlisa dikoloto — HA SE NNETE! Dula o kgutlisa.

misconceptions.english: Borrowing is always bad — FALSE! Sometimes it helps.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ho alima ho mpe kamehla — HA SE NNETE! Ka nako e nngwe ho a thusa.

misconceptions.english: Only adults can borrow — FALSE! But always ask parents first.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ke batho ba baholo feela ba ka alimang — HA SE NNETE! Empa dula o botsa batswadi pele.

misconceptions.english: Student loans are free money — FALSE! They must be repaid.
misconceptions.sesotho: Dikoloto tsa baithuti ke chelete ya mahala — HA SE NNETE! Di tlameha ho kgutliswa.

misconceptions.english: No need to read loan terms — FALSE! Always understand full cost.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ha ho hlokahale ho bala dipehelo tsa kalimo — HA SE NNETE! Dula o utlwisisa theko yohle.

misconceptions.english: All debt is bad — FALSE! Education loans can be good.
misconceptions.sesotho: Molato wohle o mobe — HA SE NNETE! Dikoloto tsa thuto di ka ba ntle.

misconceptions.english: Lower rate always means cheaper loan — FALSE! Consider fees.
misconceptions.sesotho: Phaello e tlase e bolela kalimo e theko e tlase — HA SE NNETE! Nahana ka ditefiso.

misconceptions.english: Defaulting has no consequences — FALSE! It damages credit.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ho se lefe ha ho na ditlamorao — HA SE NNETE! Ho senya mokitlane.

misconceptions.english: Perfect credit needed for any loan — FALSE! Options exist.
misconceptions.sesotho: Ho hlokahala mokitlane o phethahetseng — HA SE NNETE! Ho na le dikgetho.

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to know if you should borrow money?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho tseba hore na o lokela ho alima?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Should we talk about student loans?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na re bue ka dikoloto tsa baithuti?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to understand interest on loans?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho utlwisisa phaello ya dikoloto?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Should we learn how to repay loans?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na re ithute ho kgutlisa dikoloto?

follow_up_suggestions.english: Want to know the risks of borrowing?
follow_up_suggestions.sesotho: Na o batla ho tseba dikotsi tsa ho alima?

how_to.english: Always ask a parent or teacher before borrowing.
how_to.sesotho: Dula o botsa motswadi pele o alima.

how_to.english: Only borrow what you can pay back.
how_to.sesotho: Alima feela seo o ka se kgutlisang.

how_to.english: Pay back loans as soon as you can.
Compare loan offers from different lenders.
Understand total cost including interest and fees.
Read loan terms carefully before signing.
how_to.sesotho: Bala dipehelo ka hloko pele o saena.
Bala debt-to-income ratio pele o alima.

why.english: Understanding loans helps you avoid debt problems.
why.sesotho: Ho utlwisisa ho qoba mathata a molato.

why.english: Always repay loans to build trust.
why.sesotho: Dula o kgutlisa ho haha tshepo.

why.english: Borrowing wisely can help you achieve goals.
why.sesotho: Ho alima ka bohlale ho thusa dipakane.

why.english: Loans can help pay for education.
why.sesotho: Dikoloto di thusa ho lefella thuto.

why.english: Good debt vs bad debt matters.
why.sesotho: Molato o motle vs o mobe o bohlokwa.

why.english: Loans enable education and business investment.
why.sesotho: Dikoloto di dumella thuto le kgwebo.
Ho utlwisisa ho thibela ho alima ka bomadimabe.

why.english: Debt management is key to financial health.

situation.english: Your friend borrows M20 and promises to pay back M25 next week. Is this a good deal for you?
situation.sesotho: Motswalle o alima M20 mme o tshepisa ho kgutlisa M25 bekeng e tlang. Na ke ntho e ntle?

advice.english: Yes, M5 extra is interest. But always be careful lending to friends.
advice.sesotho: E, M5 e eketsehileng ke phaello. Empa dula o hlokolosi ha o alima metswalle.

lesson.english: Interest is earned when you lend money too.
lesson.sesotho: Phaello e fumanwa le ha o alima chelete.

situation.english: You need M5,000 for school fees. Two options: Borrow from bank at 8% for 1 year, or from a loan shark at 30% for 6 months. Which is safer?
situation.sesotho: O hloka M5,000 bakeng sa ditefello. Banka 8% selemo, kapa loan shark 30% dikgwedi tse 6. E feng e bolokehileng?

advice.english: Bank: M5,400 total. Loan shark: M5,750 total. Bank is cheaper and safer.
advice.sesotho: Banka: M5,400. Loan shark: M5,750. Banka e theko e tlase le e bolokehileng.

lesson.english: Avoid loan sharks with extremely high interest rates.
lesson.sesotho: Qoba loan sharks tse nang le diphaello tse phahameng haholo.

situation.english: You graduate with M20,000 student loan at 10% over 5 years. Monthly payment is M425. Is this manageable on a M4,000 salary?
situation.sesotho: O qeta ka kalimo ya M20,000 ka 10% dilemo tse 5. Tefo ya kgwedi M425. Na see se a kgoneha ka moputso wa M4,000?

advice.english: M425 is about 10.6% of income — manageable. But reduce other expenses.
advice.sesotho: M425 ke 10.6% ya moputso — ea kgoneha. Empa fokotsa ditshenyehelo tse ding.

lesson.english: Keep debt payments under 15% of monthly income.
lesson.sesotho: Boloka ditefo tsa molato ka tlasa 15% ya moputso.
